newsitem.title: USA: GM, Ford top UAW's list for contract talks - NYT.
newsitem.headline: GM, Ford top UAW's list for contract talks - NYT.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union is leaning toward negotiating a new national labour contract first at the General Motors Corp and the Ford Motor Co, The New York Times reported on Tuesday.
The union would thus leave Chrysler Corp for later.

Although UAW president Steve Yokich could change his mind, the union's current consensus is that talks should proceed simultaneously with Ford and GM, people familiar with the union's decision-making told the newspaper.
The three-year labour contracts between the UAW and each of the Big Three auto makers expire at midnight on September 14.

Although Yokich and Richard Shoemaker, the UAW's vice president for GM issues, are delegates to the Democratic National Convention in Chicago, both men stayed in Detroit to work out strategy, the sources said.
Another delegate, Ernest Lofton, the UAW's vice president for Ford issues, flew back to Detroit on Monday to join them.

A fourth delegate, Jack Laskowski, the vice president and head of Chrysler issues, remained in Chicago, a sign that Chrysler is unlikely to be included in the UAW's first round of negotiations, the newspaper said.
